newsitem.title: PERU: Profit-taking ends Lima bolsa's run of gains.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking ends Lima bolsa's run of gains.

text.p: Profit-taking, especially in the mining sector, ended a five-session run of gains on the Lima Stock Exchange and pushed the main indexes down by the close.
Market analysts predicted that tendency would continue Wednesday.

According to preliminary figures, the bolsa's General Index fell 0.86 percent Tuesday to 2,237.49 points while the blue-chip Selective Index lost 1.38 percent to 3,217.54. Volume was a healthy 54 million soles ($21 million) on 2,801 trades.

"Investors collected profits from the polymetallic companies since the international price of zinc is now almost static around $1,440 per tonne," said Renzo Benavides, broker for Finvest. "However, the (mining) sector still has positive perspectives."
Polymetallic miner Milpo lost 7.00 percent to 46.5 soles, Perubar was off 5.82 percent to 8.90 soles and Atacocha fell 4.51 percent to 2.75 soles.
"The perspectives for the bolsa are good, but it is logical that investors give themselves a breather and make sure of their profits," added broker Percy Romero of Fortuna brokerage.

Bucking the trend, winners included Cementos Lima, up 10 percent to 6.05 soles on expectations of announcements at Tuesday's board meeting, ice cream and confectionery firm D'Onofrio, which rose 1.68 percent to 1.21 soles, and electric utility Luz del Sur, which gained 0.32 percent to 3.11 soles.
